Eona: The national champions went 14-3, beating Ranroman State 30-14 in the Great Fourteen final and Dietsche 56-24 at Palm Creek after a 31-28 semifinal win over Tasson. Four first-round picks left, defensive lineman Nanami Sasagawa at No. 8, linebacker Emeka Belloni, running back Kyriaki Chrypoulos and lineman Demetrius Akisei, among 11 draftees in all. Hollis Upshaw's fifth year brings in five-star lineman Tyrell Kingsmond and quarterback Petr Velenko from Costique State, and Dietsche comes to Eona in week 3 in a rematch of the title game.
Ranroman State: An 11-4 year ended in the quarterfinals, 34-17 to Pistolheart at the Lumber Bowl, after a 30-14 loss to Eona in the Great Fourteen final and a 55-7 second-round win over Marblehead. Defensive lineman Omar Geortellis went fifth overall. Litowa Mesteniy's fourth year starts at home against Skeenerland State in week 0, adds five-star quarterback Dulce Navamayor and transfer quarterback Adelheid Solland from Kaji Kita State, and ends with Pistolheart at home in week 13 and a trip to Ranroman in week 14.
Dietsche: A 15-2 season took Dietsche to the national title game: a 42-23 win over Tasson in the Jyras Bay final, then wins over Trapper Point, Hoganelle and Pistolheart before the 56-24 loss to Eona. Sora Yamamoto's fifth year keeps the same coordinators, Itsuki Tachibana and Baltazar Albamayor, each also in a fifth year. Five-star linebacker Uchenna Zamorano is the headline freshman and punter Magnus Apotzis arrives from Coachville. The schedule includes a week-3 trip to Eona and Antiragal State in week 7.
Rogaela State: An 8-4 year, 5-4 in Jyras Bay play, missed the postseason. Rami Campbell is in his 16th year, but the offense changes hands: Carlos Lopez left to coordinate the defense at Central Stanton, and Brunhilde Stanhope arrives from Kaji Daun as offensive coordinator. Five-star linebacker Howahkan Laufanua leads a class of 18. Dietsche is the week-14 finale.
Barhold: An 11-4 year ended in the quarterfinals, 38-17 to Tasson at the Redwood Bowl, after wins over Vaughn Bay State (41-10) and UFNH (48-23). Cornerback Adjoa Ezesah went 28th overall. Darnell Ellery's fourth year has a new defensive coordinator in Ettore Albareal and five-star lineman Ghislaine Vignascio in the class. Skeenerland State visits in week 6 and Barhold goes to Marblehead in week 7.
Park Island: An 11-3 year, 8-1 in Western Coast play, ended with a 33-31 loss to Yrei Trobniy in the conference final and a 34-23 second-round loss to Hoganelle. Svetlana Wright's fifth year has a new defensive coordinator in Poppy Hollerbach, and five-star lineman Dieter Eisenhuber heads a class of 17. The season opens at home against Orlot in week 0 and closes with Burrstone; Yrei Trobniy is a week-13 trip.
Crayellan: A 9-6 year was a playoff run: Crayellan beat Fiota Bay 27-20 in the Mountain Valley final, beat Hatesei 17-14 in round one, and lost to Eona 36-27 in the second round. Ximena Carrasco's sixth year has Axel Osterberg in as defensive coordinator, and safety Sunita Gangaraj went 36th overall as an early entrant. A week-3 trip to Tasson and a week-9 trip to Fiota Bay are the marquee road games.
Pistolheart: An 11-4 year, 6-3 in the Great Fourteen, reached the semifinals: wins over Yrei Trobniy (35-20) and Ranroman State (34-17), then a 28-13 loss to Dietsche at the Steam Bowl. Pistolheart is still looking for its first national title. Ten players were drafted, including lineman Honoka Harukami at No. 25. Tage Ludendorf's third year brings five-star tight end Mireille Ashwell, and the schedule is among the hardest on this list, with Ranroman State away in week 13 and Central Stanton at home in week 14.
North Hatesei: The most decorated program in the country, with 21 titles and the latest in 2030, went 7-5 and missed the postseason. Perla Notaro arrives as head coach after being poached from Eternal Fox, where she went 8-5. Wide receiver Ikaika Highknife comes in from Costique State, and the class is small, 11. Eona visits in week 6 and the season closes at home against Hatesei.
Ranroman: An 8-5 year ended in round one, 30-24 at home to Yrei Trobniy. Offensive coordinator Vika Lameotter left to become head coach at Orlot and Adelheid Ostrenko takes over the offense for Ghislaine Penahermosa's third year. Running back Zlata Radushkin transfers in from Kaji Daun. The year opens at Will Tech in week 0, goes to Eona in week 11 and ends at home against Ranroman State.
Central Stanton: A 7-5 year, 6-3 in the Great Fourteen, missed the postseason. Boris Walker is in his ninth year and Carlos Lopez arrives from Rogaela State as defensive coordinator. The recruiting class is only five players, led by five-star linebacker Kanei Lorresei. The finish is demanding: Eona in week 13 and a trip to Pistolheart in week 14.
Tengus State: A 7-5 year, 6-3 in Power North play, missed the postseason. Layla Smith is in a 15th year; lineman Palmira Zambrano went 16th overall and linebacker Amara Amateng 21st. Quarterback Peizhi Liangyan comes in from Costique. The schedule opens with Diamond City in week 2 and goes to Barhold in week 4 and Skeenerland State in week 11.
Eastern State: The 2040 champions went 8-4, 5-4 in Broad South play, and missed the postseason; only one player was drafted. Bhaskar El-Mahdi's third year adds four-star quarterback Heriberto Holmhus. Ekralund State visits in week 6, Eastern State goes to Ciarralotta Tech in week 7 and finishes at Keeper.
Skylar Rose: The 2041 champions went 8-4 and missed the postseason. Amir Chen is in his seventh year; defensive lineman Maximo Penalarga went 54th and lineman Svyatoslav Jasnanov 60th. Hatesei is the week-1 visitor, Park Island is a week-10 trip, and Southern Tengus is the finale at home.
Hatesei: A 9-4 year ended in round one, 17-14 at home to Crayellan. Freya Dahlqvist's second year faces the second-hardest schedule of the 152 programs, opening at Skylar Rose in week 1, going to Eona in week 4 and ending at North Hatesei. Safety Auvenniy Mesreniy went 31st overall and quarterback Elharith Geortzis comes in from Chinolka.
Tasson: A 13-3 year included a 9-0 run through Jyras Bay play, a 42-23 loss to Dietsche in the conference final, wins over Canesta State (35-17) and Barhold (38-17), and a 31-28 semifinal loss to Eona at the Star Bowl. Andre Hernandez's fifth year has a new offensive coordinator in Jadwiga Bergkamp. Receiver Snezana Wolfbruck arrives from Antiragal State and five-star receiver Clive Neubonne leads the class. Crayellan visits in week 3 and Antiragal State in week 6.
Yrei Trobniy: A 10-5 year began with a 33-31 win over Park Island in the Western Coast final, then a 30-24 round-one win at Ranroman and a 35-20 loss to Pistolheart in round two. Quarterback Sungmin Zhenbin went tenth overall as an early entrant, and Wei Lanyuan transfers in from Holliday. Hollis Heathcote's fifth year hosts Park Island in week 13 and ends at Good River.
UNN: An 8-4 year, 6-3 in the Great Fourteen, missed the postseason. Esperanza Caraobruno's fifth year keeps both coordinators, and quarterback Douglas Kingsworth returns as a junior. The schedule is the 12th hardest of the 152 programs, with Central Stanton away in week 7, Ranroman at home in week 8 and Eona the week-14 visitor.
UFNH: A 9-4 year ended in the second round, 48-23 to Barhold. Offensive coordinator Hanan Mukhopadhyay left to become head coach at Queensville and Bushra Al-Saadi takes over the offense in Moritz Lamehawk's third year. Defensive lineman Afamasaga Claycroft went third overall. The year includes a week-8 trip to Crayellan and finishes at home against Fiota Bay.
Skeenerland State: An 8-4 year, 6-3 in Power North play, missed the postseason, and defensive coordinator Kojo Rowbrook left to become head coach at Kaji Kita. Ji-woo Hall is in his 13th year with Aliyah Radovsky taking over the defense. The portal was busy: receivers Hannelore Birkelund and Bertram Ravikanth, kicker Salma Ibekwe and quarterback Marco Veganegro all arrive. The season opens at Ranroman State in week 0.
Black Forest: The only Low Sixteen team in the top 25 went 12-2, beating Westburg 18-0 in the conference final before a 31-10 loss to Canesta State in round one. Salma Park is in a ninth year and keeps both coordinators. Five-star lineman Nadine Trianakis headlines the class and safety Jongdae Ju-Ho arrives from Vaughn Bay State. The schedule is among the softest, with trips to Ciarralotta State in week 2 and Eona Navy in week 9 the notable non-conference tests.
Antiragal State: A 9-3 year, 7-2 in Jyras Bay play, missed the postseason, and three early entrants were drafted: defensive linemen Alofa Matatalo and Harumi Yawdele and receiver Tallulah Spottedcrane. Receiver Snezana Wolfbruck left for Tasson. Xavier Byun is in his 14th year, with Tasson away in week 6 and Dietsche at home in week 7.
Marblehead: A 10-5 year began with a 28-24 win over Diveo State in the Power North final and a 32-28 round-one win over Rogaela, then ended with a 55-7 loss to Ranroman State. Receiver Terrell Highcombe went fourth overall. Onawa Khan is in a 14th year, with transfer quarterback Varun Balaraj from Stanton State; Barhold visits in week 7.
Kaji Daun: A 6-6 year, 3-6 in the Great Fourteen, missed the postseason, and offensive coordinator Brunhilde Stanhope left for Rogaela State. Henrik Moreau's third year has Youngchul Otonashi running the offense; running back Lucia Pellatelli went 30th overall and Zlata Radushkin transferred to Ranroman. The schedule is the third hardest of the 152 programs, with Eona at home in week 9 and Kaji Kita the week-14 finale.
Lornaman: An 11-4 year began with a 24-23 win over Keeper in the Broad South final and a 26-7 round-one win over UN Minko, and ended with a 34-17 loss to Fiota Bay in round two. Quarterback Uili Quickbear went 61st as an early entrant. Henry Sandcombe's fifth year keeps both coordinators, with five-star linebacker Dragana Georpoulos in the class and trips to Eastern State in week 9 and Ciarralotta Tech in week 13.
